title: Borrowed References, Local Languages: Blended Styles on Latin American Façades
text:
Borrowed References, Local Languages: Blended Styles on Latin American Façades

Architectural styles are often identified through a familiar set of characteristics: particular forms, materials, proportions, and decorative elements. Yet these characteristics do not always remain tied to the traditions from which they originate. A classical column may appear on a self-built house, a modernist ceramic composition may be reproduced across a residential façade, or a chalet may become part of a multistory commercial building. Each retains something recognizable from its precedent, although its application reflects a different set of architectural decisions.

title: "What Other Forms of Architecture Might Exist?": In Conversation With Participants at the 2026 Sharjah Architecture Triennial
text:
"What Other Forms of Architecture Might Exist?": In Conversation With Participants at the 2026 Sharjah Architecture Triennial

The third edition of the Sharjah Architecture Triennial (SAT03), titled Architecture Otherwise: Building Civic Infrastructure for Collective Futures, brings together practitioners exploring architecture beyond conventional building practices. During the opening week, ArchDaily's Editor-in-Chief Christele Harrouk spoke with Makram el Kadi and Ziad Jamaleddine of L.E.FT, Mohamad Nahleh, Khondaker Hasibul Kabir and Suhailey Farzana of POCAA, May al-Ibrashy of Megawra-BEC, Nathalie Harb and Mohamad Hafeda, and Hamed Bukhamseen and Ali İsmail Karimi of Civil Architecture about their contributions, which engage with spiritual practices, community-led spatial production, heritage, displacement, and material reuse. Through installations, collective research, and interventions in existing spaces, their work considers how architecture can emerge through different forms of knowledge, care, and engagement with everyday life.

title: London Museum Opens in Smithfield’s General Market on November 28
text:
London Museum Opens in Smithfield’s General Market on November 28

London Museum opens in its new home in West Smithfield's restored General Market on Saturday, November 28. The institution, formerly known as the Museum of London, closed its previous location at 150 London Wall, near the Barbican complex, on December 4, 2022. The relocation project has taken a decade to bring the collections representing the city's story, from the prehistoric inhabitants who settled by the Thames to today's global city, to a newly restored historic building. Stanton Williams led the transformation of the General Market, with collaborating architect Asif Khan Studio and conservation architects Julian Harrap Architects. According to Director Sharon Ament, the project is a collective endeavor that tells "the city's story in all its grit and glitter."

title: From Policy to Pavement: Preparing Cities for El Niño in the Greater Horn of Africa
text:
From Policy to Pavement: Preparing Cities for El Niño in the Greater Horn of Africa

To limit the toll of El Niño's October-December rains, IGAD's specialized climate institution, the Climate Prediction and Applications Centre (ICPAC), has released a practical guide with UN-Habitat for Horn of Africa cities. The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) is a regional bloc in Eastern Africa of governments from the Greater Horn of Africa, and their High-Level Call to Action on El Niño Preparedness establishes a regional commitment to move from reactive disaster response to proactive action for long-term resilience. Emphasizing cross-border coordination and crediting local knowledge, the call states: "We recognize that climate and disaster risks do not respect national borders, and that no single country or institution can manage them alone."

title: Jiujiang Ferry Cultural Complex Renovation / TURTLEHILL DESIGN
text:
Jiujiang Ferry Cultural Complex Renovation / TURTLEHILL DESIGN

The abandoned ferry terminal along the Xijiang River in Jiujiang Town, Foshan, once served as a vital dock connecting the riverine islands. With the commissioning of a new terminal, this structure—imbued with memories of waterway transportation—gradually fell into disuse, leaving only a concrete skeleton and steps leading to a decaying pier. Situated at the intersection of a wetland park and a residential area, the site combines ecological sensitivity with community service potential. The design team faced the challenge of transforming this ruin into a multifunctional public space—integrating a bookstore, exhibition hall, café, cultural events, and art performances—within a footprint of less than 150 square meters, while responding to the climatic characteristics of the Pearl River Delta and the region's industrial cultural context.

title: Fenix Art Museum / MAD Architects
text:
Fenix Art Museum / MAD Architects

Fenix is a major new museum that explores migration through the lens of art, opening on a landmark site in Rotterdam's City Harbor, developed by internationally acclaimed architects MAD. With a rapidly expanding collection of historic and contemporary objects, Fenix tells the story of migration through a series of encounters with art, architecture, photography, food, and history. Located in what was once part of the world's largest transshipment warehouse, on a peninsula in Rotterdam's historic port district, Fenix overlooks the docks where millions of migrant journeys began and ended. The monumental 16,000 square meter warehouse has been transformed to become Fenix by MAD Architects with restoration consultation by Bureau Polderman. This is MAD Architects' first commission for a public cultural building in Europe, as well as the first museum to be built by a Chinese firm in Europe. The project was initiated by the Droom en Daad Foundation, founded in 2016. The Foundation is helping redefine Rotterdam for the 21st century - developing new kinds of arts and culture institutions and fostering new creative talent that reflects the city's diversity, its spirit, and its history

The façades of untreated timber change with the weather, the light and the seasons, making the passing of time visible to the children.

title: Japanese Perspectives
text:
Japanese Perspectives

Japanese Perspectives, published by Distanz Verlag, Berlin, explores architectural responses to resource scarcity, demographic change, and climate adaptation through the lens of contemporary Japan.
Bringing together essays by Japanese architects, selected projects and observations from everyday urban life, the book examines practices of reuse, transformation, and working with existing structures.
The contributions reveal an architectural culture in which tradition and innovation, continuity and change, are continuously negotiated—inviting a reconsideration of architecture as a cultural practice of adaptation and renewal.

title: Does Your Building Work or Does It Just Photograph Well? What Neuroscience and Use Data Could Teach Architects
text:
Does Your Building Work or Does It Just Photograph Well? What Neuroscience and Use Data Could Teach Architects

Architecture reaches people through whatever medium carries it, and each new medium changes our picture of what a good building looks like. For example, when 3D modeling software arrived, the novelty of complex shapes drove the starchitecture era of the 2010s, and projects built on those experiments earned awards such as the Pritzker Prize. Today the medium is the social media feed. A building exists first as a model and then as a render, long before it exists as a place. Meanwhile, research in neuroarchitecture is building a different picture based on how people actually experience buildings. So how could those two seemingly unrelated topics close a loop that may lead to the profession's next creative frontier?
